notes:
Method: recomputed every ratio, share, delta and sum in the chapter from the chapter's own published values, then cross-checked the two ledgers against the figure's backing series (figuras/aic/aic_fn_engines_aiccurve.csv and figuras_new/aic_fn.html) purely to adjudicate whether a prose number had a referent. No provenance DB was consulted.

ADJUDICATION OF THE EXTRACTOR'S THREE FLAGS: (1) the 1.43x caption value is REFUTED as an arithmetic error -- the figure genuinely extends to N=128, where 1033.208/723.514 = 1.428; the real defect is that the caption calls N=128 'the largest dispatch' while the body reserves 'dispatch cap' for N=64 (recorded as an ambiguity, finding 6). (2) The 0.25 vs 1.18 ms elementwise discrepancy is CONFIRMED and is the chapter's most consequential defect, because it is what breaks the 'no unexplained residual' claim (findings 1 and 3). (3) The 0.26 vs 0.248 DeepStack pair is CONFIRMED but is not a rounding error of one number -- the two sections quote two different profiling runs (0.257 and 0.248); the same run-to-run split shows up more strongly in the patch-embedding convolution (0.459 vs 0.495, 7.8% apart) and in the total kernel time (9.624 vs a 9.542 figure-ledger sum), which the extractor did not catch (finding 7).

The extractor's separate claim that the N=8 residual should be -2.1% is CONFIRMED only against the rounded 43.1 printed in that sentence; it is correct to -2.2% against the table's 43.13, so it is recorded as a rounding/presentation defect rather than a wrong number (finding 13).

HIGHEST RISK REMAINING: the 12.8% headline bound rests on a single dense-sweep maximum of +12.7% at N=52, only 0.1pp of margin, and is asserted five times (lines 248, 262, 317, 352, 517). Appendix~\ref{app:engine-sensitivity} reportedly states 'within 11.4%' for the same comparison -- a cross-file conflict that this chapter-internal pass cannot settle and that the cross-chapter pass should resolve.

NOT INTERNALLY CHECKABLE (no defect asserted): the 120/120 rho=20 feasibility grid and the six-window 6-8 worker sizing (line 357-359); the encoder-delay p99 triple 589/606/644 ms; burst5's 8-vs-16 worker correction; the 3.1% extrapolated trace share; the 1157/276/17 shape counts; the 465-case infill composition; the dense sweep's 69 batch sizes and +21.8% at N=512; the 27.6 req/s and 32.4 ms TTFT smoke-test pair (offered load is 50 req/s at a 20 ms interval, but completion rate is decode-bound and no decode length is published, so the pair is under-determined rather than contradictory).
